claims.text: Catalytic activity of transition-metal catalysts is governed by the electronic structure of the metal.
The d-band center relative to the Fermi level influences the adsorption strength of reactants and intermediates.
Alloying a transition metal with another element can modify its d-band center.
Applying lattice strain can modify the d-band center of a transition-metal catalyst.
The position of the d-band center relative to the Fermi level affects the binding energy of surface reactants and intermediates.
Changes in the binding energies of reactants and intermediates influence catalytic activity.
A d-band center closer to the Fermi level typically increases adsorption strength.
A d-band center farther from the Fermi level typically decreases adsorption strength.
For reactions requiring strong intermediate adsorption, catalysts with d-band centers closer to the Fermi level will exhibit higher activity.
Catalysts with d-band centers farther from the Fermi level will have lower activity or higher selectivity in reactions requiring weaker adsorption.
The proposed relationship is limited to reactions in which adsorption strength is a critical determinant of activity or selectivity.
The proposed relationship is limited to transition metals with partially filled d orbitals.
The quantitative relationship between d-band center and activity or selectivity may depend on the reaction and on the identities of reactants and intermediates.
A lack of correlation between measured d-band-center position and catalytic activity and selectivity would falsify the hypothesis.
